dataset_family: National Taiwan University Hospital memory clinics plus local community controls, Taipei (single site; 87 older adults, analysed 36 HC-NA / 24 MCI-NA / 22 MCI-PA)
method_family: Diffusion spectrum imaging (102 directions, bmax 4000) with tract-based automatic analysis (tract mGFA), plus FreeSurfer regional and global morphometry
what_it_shows: Chang et al. 2021, NeuroImage Clin 30:102626. Both MCI groups show lower left-fornix mGFA than controls with normal awareness (HC-NA) (p = .009 and p = .045). The poor-awareness MCI subgroup (MCI-PA) also has lower mGFA than HC-NA in the dorsal frontal-striatal tracts, the left anterior thalamocortical radiation-ventral part, and the callosal fibres to the ventral prefrontal cortex and inferior parietal lobule; MCI-NA does not differ from HC-NA on those tracts. Global total cerebral GM (p = 0.10) and WM (p = 0.91) volumes do not differ among the groups. The regional static measures the authors pre-selected DO separate both MCI groups from HC-NA: bilateral hippocampal volume (right p = .02 / .003, left p = .032 / .008) and right frontal cortical thickness (p = .01 / .03).
why: Partly. The part it shows: a tract-level diffusion measure separates MCI from a matched non-impaired comparator in the same participants where the global macrostructural volumes (total cerebral GM and WM) do not. The corresponding regional static measures, however, also separate. For the fornix, the one tract where BOTH MCI groups differ from controls, the natural static counterpart is hippocampal volume, and it separated both MCI groups from HC-NA, so there is no dissociation there. The best-fitting contrast is callosal-IPL mGFA (MCI-PA vs HC-NA p = .001) against IPL cortical thickness. IPL thickness is not among the regions the Results list as significant, so it apparently did not separate, but that null is inferred from its absence in the text, not from a printed statistic. That contrast is also confined to the poor-awareness subgroup (22 of 46 MCI); MCI-NA did not differ from controls on it. The authors' 'could not be explained by gray matter morphometry' refers to MCI-PA versus MCI-NA, a within-MCI contrast with no non-impaired comparator. It does not refer to MCI versus controls. Global-volume versus single-tract microstructure is also a mismatch of spatial scale. Further limits: brain analyses use uncorrected p < 0.05; HC-NA is a selected subset of controls (36 of 41, poor-awareness controls excluded); MCI was defined at -1 SD, a mild sample. No shared cohort, site or authors with any current supporter (Chongqing, Wuhan, Guangzhou, UT Dallas/Southwestern, Shanghai) or with the other candidates. Not a preprint.

quotes.quote: Table 1, Macro-Brain Variables: 'Total cerebral gray matter (cm3) 586.88 (43.04) 575.68(44.72) 560.06 (48.77) 0.10 Total cerebral white matter (cm3) 414.37 (44.46) 409.42 (43.89) 410.82(46.63) 0.91' (HC-NA, MCI-NA, MCI-PA, p)

The global measures of the total cerebral gray matter, cerebral white matter, and eTIV volumes did not differ significantly among the groups (all p values > 0.05, Table 1). Compared with the HC-NA group, the MCI-NA and MCI-PA groups demonstrated decreased right frontal cortical thickness (F(2,79) = 4.30, p = .017; p = .01, Cohen's d = 0.71 vs. p = .03, Cohen's d = 0.60), right hippocampal volume (F(2,79) = 5.46, p = .006; p = .02, Cohen's d = 0.61 vs. p = .003, Cohen's d = 0.85), and left hippocampal volume (F(2,79) = 4.49, p = .014; p = .032, Cohen's d = 0.62 vs. p = .008, Cohen's d = 0.71).

Post hoc analyses revealed that the MCI-NA and MCI-PA groups exhibited lower mGFA values for the left fornix than the HC-NA group did (p = .009, Cohen's d = 0.81 vs. p = .045, Cohen's d = 0.53); however, the mGFA values did not differ between the two MCI groups.

Compared with the HC-NA and MCI-NA groups, the MCI-PA group had a lower mGFA value of the left dorsal frontal-striatal tract (p = .019, Cohen's d = 0.59 vs. p = .023, Cohen's d = 0.57), right dorsal frontal-striatal tract (p = .016, Cohen's d = 0.64 vs. p = .032, Cohen's d = 0.56), left anterior thalamocortical radiations-ventral part (p = .014, Cohen's d = 0.67 vs. p = .040, Cohen's d = 0.54), and corpus callosum-inferior parietal lobule (p = .001, Cohen's d = 0.76 vs. p = .003, Cohen's d = 0.83).

Moreover, the MCI group with poor memory awareness exhibited decreased white matter integrity for the bilateral dorsal frontal-striatal tract, left anterior thalamocortical radiations-ventral part, and corpus callosum connecting the bilateral inferior parietal lobule and ventral prefrontal regions. This result could not be explained by morphometric differences in gray matter.

Given the relatively small sample size and to achieve a balance between the rigorous control of the potential confounding covariate and the ability to detect meaningful findings, the alpha level was set as the conventional significance threshold (p < 0.05) for all the statistical analyses involving brain variables
